shadow:
A small weight rides above a serious life, a low grey cloud that follows wherever the day goes. It is the sense that something is owed, that the next thing has to be gripped before it slips, that the wrong outcome is always one slack moment away. Seriousness is not the same as caring deeply. It is caring while clenched.

It lives in the body before it ever reaches a thought. The shoulders carry it. The breath goes shallow and stays there. A person can be in a beautiful room, with food on the table and people who love them, and still feel the day as a problem being managed rather than a life being lived.

Most people read this weight as proof they should try harder, plan further, hold on tighter. That reading is the trap, because the holding on is what makes the day go wrong. Things stop arriving on time. Luck seems to fall to other people.

The way out is hidden in how the grip works. Squeeze tighter and the world squirms loose. Loosen the hand even slightly and something starts to move. The body already knows this. It is waiting for permission to set the day down.
repressive: Some people meet the seriousness by going cold inside their own skin. They stop reaching for touch or taste or pleasure, decide their body is a thing to manage and not to enjoy, and let a quiet frost settle over the senses. It reads as composure. It is not.
reactive: Others meet it by performing lightness. They laugh loudly, treat nothing as it matters, keep the jokes coming so no one looks too close. Scratch that surface and you find someone wound very tight, with old anger sitting just under the easy grin.
gift:
Something loosens when a person stops bracing against the day and starts owning it instead. The frost over the senses thaws. What was being held off, the ordinary texture of being alive in a body, becomes something to step toward.

That thaw is delight. It is not a mood you summon. It is what a day feels like once you stop interfering with it. Food tastes like something again. A conversation is allowed to wander. Touch is welcome rather than rationed. The body, which spent years braced, starts to relax into its own warmth.

And here the strange thing happens. As the grip eases, the day begins to cooperate. The right person turns up. The dropped thread reappears. Others call it luck and envy it, but it is closer to a knack for being where things are already about to happen. You did not arrange that. You stopped blocking it.

Delight still has goals. It works, it builds, it wants things. It just holds them loosely enough that they can be put down if the day offers something better. That last part is what most people cannot do, which is exactly why it works.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the lightness is no longer something a person practices. It is the temperature they live at. The mind that used to stand over every moment grading it has gone quiet, not forced quiet, just no longer needed. It speaks when there is something to do and falls still the rest of the time.

This is ecstasy, and it has nothing to do with leaving the world. It happens at the table, in the marketplace, between two people who are simply glad to be near each other. It comes in waves, the way wind moves through a garden, swelling and dipping, never holding one note for long.

The body turns out to have been the doorway all along. The same body that once carried the grey weight is the instrument the joy plays through. From here a person can look back at all that early seriousness, the clenching, the worry that the day would go wrong. It was not a flaw. It was the closed hand learning, slowly, how to open.
